title: Ethosuximide in WWOX-related epilepsy
summary: One mouse study reported an effect on experimentally induced seizures after ethosuximide pretreatment. The result leaves WWOX specificity, spontaneous seizure control and benefit in children with WWOX-DEE unestablished.
evidence: Cheng and colleagues reported suppression of PTZ-provoked seizure activity in Wwox-null mice in Figure 7B. LEGEND's re-reading of the plotted group means found that the separation was mostly late in the observation period. The graph does not supply the individual trajectories needed to resolve the uncertainty of that time-window comparison.
Clinical evidence for childhood absence epilepsy concerns a different seizure syndrome. It cannot substitute for a WWOX-DEE study.
limits: The mouse study did not establish a treatment-by-genotype interaction. A result detected in one genotype and not in another is insufficient to establish specificity. Baseline differences and low seizure scores in the comparator arms also limit interpretation.
The study does not identify which T-type calcium channel, if any, mediated the result. It does not establish an effect on spontaneous seizures or on development in WWOX-DEE.
research_question: Would the effect persist in an age-matched comparison with interpretable baseline activity in each genotype, and would it extend to spontaneous events? Measuring a treatment-by-genotype interaction would help distinguish WWOX-specific effects from general seizure suppression.

sources.label: Cheng et al. Wwox deficiency and seizure susceptibility in mice, Figure 7B. PMID 32000863.
